newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Lira set to rejoin ERM, London shares rocket.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Lira set to rejoin ERM, London shares rocket.

text.p: Currency traders focused on the lira on Friday after Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said it would return to the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) in a matter of "a few hours or a few days."
The other key feature in Europe was the strong rise in London shares which had stormed to a 1.32 percent gain by 1530 GMT.
The lira firmed to around 996 to the mark after starting the day at around 1000, only to fall back to around 999 by 1515 GMT after news broke that Italy had sought re-entry to Europe's currency grid.
Antonio Fazio, governor of the Bank of Italy, confirmed that the Rome government had asked for the Italian lira to be readmitted to the ERM. It crashed out of the grid in 1992.
A senior banking source in Frankfurt said that Rome had requested a European Union monetary meeting in Brussels on Saturday to discuss the lira's re-entry.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, stormed back up above the 4,000 mark as initial gains in utility and power stocks energised other sectors and pushed worries about interest rates and next week's budget into the background.

Gainers outnumbered losers by 83 to 13 in a respectable volume of 500 million shares as a wave of short covering engulfed a market many had expected to languish before Tuesday's British budget as investors fretted about the strong pound and inflation.
"One or two marketmakers got caught a bit short of stock today. They are squealing, they are losing money," one senior trader said.

Another, confessing surprise at the FTSE's new-found strength said: "There were one or two institutions telling me this morning they thought the market was going to lift off and test all-time highs in the near future."

Dealers said the market, in the doldrums for most of this week as investors debated whether Chancellor Kenneth Clarke would be tempted into pre-election tax cuts, was growing more confident the budget would be fiscally prudent.

Utility and energy stocks led the market, with nuclear electricity generator British Energy hitting new highs on a favourable write-up in the Financial Times on the company's cash generating strength.

British Energy, London's fourth most-active share with over 13 million stocks changing hands, was up 10p at 144-1/2p, by midafternoon. Other generators gained, notably PowerGen, up 7-1/2p at 594p and National Power, up 18p at 469p.
In Paris, French shares defied early profit-taking at the end of the account to push to a year high above 2,250.
Traders said the market was well-oriented, with a firm trend on the dollar and debt markets. London's surge through the 4,000 level was also supportive.

A current round of group restructurings and acquisitions made sense as companies could boost earnings per share by buying in minority interests, helped with short-term interest rates at around 3.5 percent, said one broker.
The market was also buoyed by the prospect of fresh inflows as private pensions seemed likely to appear next year, after many years of debate and delay.

German shares ended fairly thin-volume bourse dealings 0.3 percent weaker after Wall Street closed lower overnight, with dealers saying the market was taking a breather following recent bullish trading.
"We're just seeing a small correction," said one dealer. Trade is really quiet. But things have generally been busier in the afternoons this week so the market could pick up."
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 111.25 yen and 1.5025 marks against 111.43 yen and 1.4980 marks late on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 52.6 points at 4,006.4.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 14.01 points at 2,247.58.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 8.65 points at 2,763.69.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $377.00 Gold in the afternoon compared with Thursday's close of $376.65.
